Triangulation between the clear view in LASCO C3 and faint, difficult to resolve view in STEREO A COR2. Despite the source being located around W105, this front does not fit well outside of the W70-W80 range, with available imagery and its quality. Attempts to fit around W105 do not match the COR2A structure, but no other corresponding eruptions or fronts to account for this are identified, so it is possible this CME is just greatly deflected away from the source coordinates.

Updated SHOCK measurement using potential source location from STEREO A EUVI 304/195. There is a higher level of uncertainty with this analysis due to limited triangulation ability as well as the unique shape of the CME front. This analysis tracks the furthest out portion of the shock (the "nose") of the CME and includes most of the shock that is more in the ecliptic plane, however this measurement also includes unavoidable empty/dead space due to the overall shape of the shock front and the restrictions of the SWPC_CAT measuring tool.

Narrow CME with clear front in STEREO A COR2. The front in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 that possibly corresponds to this event is very faint and unclear. No clear source has been found for this CME, although there is a far-sided field line movement around 2026-05-23T02:11Z pretty clearly in SUVI 284, but the CME does not triangulate to the east limb.

data.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and as a faint N/NW partial halo in STEREO A COR2. The source is very likely former AR 14436, located around N18 and W100-W110. Observed as field line movement and loops breaking over the NW limb in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-05-23T05:18Z, and directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 as slow dimming and brightening starting around 2026-05-23T06:05Z in a wide area around former AR 14436's location. This active region is in close proximity to a large coronal hole to its southwest, possibly affecting CME propagation.

data.note: Fast CME with a brighter, narrower bulk partially obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and a fainter halo shock seen to the N in COR2A and to the NE in CCOR-1 (and initially covered by the scheduled data gap in SOHO LASCO). It is associated with the fast far-sided eruption seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO 171 and GOES SUVI 284 as fast movement of field lines and restructuring of magnetic field and as long, narrow strands of a filament in GOES SUVI 304. It is associated with type II radio burst.

data.note: CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 with an irregular front overlapping with earlier NW CMEs. The front is likely also seen to the NW in a couple of timestamps of STEREO A COR2. Its source is not clear: one source could be a minor eruption in AR 14441 (N8W68)seen at 2026-05-23T10:45 in STA EUV 304/195 seen as brightening and dimming but it is not confirmed by the fit with coronagraphs. Another source could be AR 14436 (N18W110) which has been showing signs of activity for many hours.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-05-24T20:00Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, but is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely related to some field line movement seen beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning as early as 2026-05-24T18:30Z. The field line movement can also be faintly seen well beyond the E limb in STEREO A EUVI 195. There is also a narrow feature to the E in STEREO A COR2 that could be this CME, but a good triangulated fit cannot be made between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, particularly due to the grainy image quality in COR2A. No additional source was found.

Preliminary leading edge analysis, assuming former AR 14436 (~N18W145 at this time). STEREO A COR2 observations not available due to data gap, and not yet observed in LASCO C3.

Shock front analysis with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. STEREO A COR2 not available due to a data gap. The shock front is notably irregular shaped, with a northern lobe and southern feature observed as a wide partial halo. This fit tracks the majority of the observed shock front prioritizing the northern lobe in similarity to the bulk leading edge directionality. Longitude of W145 used as the approximate source of former AR 14436; the likely source for this CME without direct observation, and as such longitude could vary between W135-W155.
